hypothesis: Loading the model in FP16 instead of FP32 will reduce peak RAM (load and inference) relative to EXP-01, roughly proportional to the halved parameter byte-width, with comparable or slightly worse CPU throughput since this CPU has no native FP16 compute acceleration.

measurement.load_time_note: warm cache (model already downloaded) — not comparable to EXP-01 cold load time

result: 12/12 success. Peak inference RAM dropped 49.5% (6.9316GB -> 3.5037GB). Peak load RAM dropped 26.8%. Throughput changed by -5.0% (effectively flat, within run-to-run noise).
conclusion: FP16 is a strictly beneficial, nearly-free optimization for this memory-constrained use case on this CPU: inference memory nearly halves with no meaningful throughput cost. This supports using FP16 as the new default precision floor for all subsequent experiments (EXP-02b INT8 onward should compare against FP16, not just FP32, since FP16 is clearly superior to FP32 for our stated goal of minimizing RAM under a strict budget).
caveats: Load time not comparable to EXP-01 (warm cache vs cold download).
Peak load RAM reduction (27%) is less than theoretical 50%, likely due to transient FP32/BF16 intermediate buffers during safetensors deserialization and cast; not yet root-caused.
Per-prompt latency variance remains high (11.9s-55.7s), consistent with EXP-01 — likely shared-CPU contention in Colab, not an FP16 artifact.
